plain_english: This is a court-appointed estate inventory for the late John Glasgow. It says he died in March, but the death-year numerals cannot be securely read in this review. The marginal court date is 4 May 1577.

Margaret, whose surname remains unresolved, is expressly his widow. She submits the inventory in the name and on behalf of Katherine and [Androw?] Glasgow, called lawful children and administrators appointed to their deceased father. The passage does not explicitly say that Margaret was those children's mother.

The estate includes cattle, a mare, sheep, oats, barley, household goods and clothing. The debts list financial associates. A separate outgoing-debt entry names Katherine Glasgow as a servant owed wages; that description alone does not demonstrate that she is the same Katherine as the named child.

The inventory accounts and opening of the confirmation are transcribed here. Continuation image 277 is present in the nested John PDF, contrary to the earlier missing-source statement; its text remains outside this opening-page review.
findings: Image 276, opening lines 7-9: widowhood and the children's paternal relationship are stated independently of executor status. The explicit 'thair said vmqle father' supports John as father; Margaret's maternity remains unstated.
Image 276, outgoing debts lines 35-38: the rent creditor's place appears consistent with Hirmenschelis; the creditor and servant names remain working readings, not proved family connections.
Image 276, line 38: the outgoing-debt total is visibly six pounds. Other account totals are not sufficiently secure to replace the older ledger numerals.

The nested PDF supplies images 276 and 277, plus a separate Andrew Hutcheson screenshot with a reused header. Source availability does not make this opening-only transcription complete; image 277 still needs its own fresh reading.
changes_from_previous: Confirms the previous distinction between Margaret's explicit widowhood and unproved maternity.
The second child's name remains Androw[?]; this fresh review does not justify silently removing its uncertainty.

confidence_statement: Fresh visual examination of image 276 and enlarged crops; existing saved reading consulted only afterwards. High confidence in widow/child/father relationship clauses and partial coverage; moderate or low confidence in bracketed names and account numerals. This is an incomplete working transcription with unresolved stretches, not a diplomatic edition. Superscripts are lowered; uncertain expanded abbreviations are bracketed; the supplied continuation has not been filled with an inferred legal formula.

observations: PDF pages 1 and 3 both carry Image 276, CC8/8/5, the Johne Glasgw download title and the same generation timestamp. Page 2 carries Image 277.
Page 1 shows the complete leaf numbered 276. Page 3 shows an irregular-edged horizontal strip marked 396A beside an older struck-through number.
No repeated underlying John lines establish a raised/lowered-flap pair, and the exact physical attachment cannot be demonstrated from the supplied photographs.
The rubric identifies the confirmation of Andro Hutchesoun: identification of the separate testament is strong, but exact surname spelling remains provisional.
Bairnis and a Johne name are visible. Their full clauses, associated identities, locality and date require closer transcription.
associated_fragment.interpretation: A supplementary view was delivered with image 276. This is a real documentary association, not evidence of accidental inclusion; it does not by itself establish a genealogical relationship.
associated_fragment.family_lead: The supplied human reading hochaine, possibly a phonetic Hutchin form, makes the Hutcheson fragment relevant to Margaret and the family network. Neither surname normalization nor a specific relationship to Andro is established.
next_steps: Transcribe the complete fragment, particularly the children and Johne clauses, without borrowing expected names from the Glasgow family.
Compare its people, places, executors and debts with John Glasgow's testament.
Ask NRS or ScotlandsPeople what the strip marked 396A represents and why it is associated with image 276; the exact attachment/export rationale is not established by these views.
